---
title: "Inspecting fitted model state"
---

Fitted models expose components with explicit numerical domains. Import their
types from `pyfixest.estimation.state`.

```{python}
import pyfixest as pf
from pyfixest.estimation.state import ModelMatrix, WithinLinearData

fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1", pf.get_data())
assert isinstance(fit.model_matrix, ModelMatrix)
assert isinstance(fit.within_data, WithinLinearData)
fit.model_matrix.dependent.head()
fit.within_data.design.shape
fit.observation_weights.values is None
```

| Access | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `model_matrix` | Formula-materialized response, regressors, FE identifiers, instruments, endogenous regressors, weights, and offsets, after sample filtering. |
| `observation_weights` | User-scale weights and their analytic or frequency interpretation. `values=None` represents an unweighted fit. |
| `within_data` | Linear and IV response/design after FE absorption, without multiplication by square-root weights. Quantile models use this domain with no FE transformation. |
| `within_data.instruments`, `within_data.endogenous` | The IV-specific within-scale roles. Only `WithinIvData` has these fields. |
| `working_state` | GLM final working response/design, working weights, linear predictor `eta`, mean `mu`, and response/working residuals. |

GLM working weights already include observation weights. Do not multiply them
by observation weights again. Formula tables retain their original domain;
solver-weighted arrays are temporary calculation inputs.

Component arrays are read-only, including selections shared across multiple
fits. Copy an array before editing it. Public formula-table access returns a
detached DataFrame, so editing it cannot change the model. Preparing a fit does
not change the writeability of the caller's data.

```{python}
design_copy = fit.within_data.design.copy()
design_copy[:] = 0
response_table = fit.model_matrix.dependent
response_table.iloc[0, 0] = 0
assert not fit.within_data.design.flags.writeable
```

Continue using `coef()`, `resid()`, `predict()`, `fixef()`, and `tidy()` for
ordinary analysis. Linear and Gaussian performance measures are completed before
formula storage is dropped, so their existing access remains available. With `store_data=False`, full formula state is omitted;
with `lean=True`, observation-sized components are omitted as well. These
access paths do not expand estimator or post-estimation support.

Storage options apply to every child of a multiple-estimation result and to IV
first stages. Execution caches and unused captured context are released after
fitting. `store_data=False` retains numerical components, formula metadata, and
supported fixed-effect coefficients; `lean=True` retains coefficient inference,
sample counts, and completed performance summaries. Lean quantile results also
retain the scalar objective value.

Operations that need omitted inputs raise `pyfixest.errors.MissingModelDataError`
with the operation, missing state, and remedy. Estimator support errors remain
separate. For example, lean results support `tidy()` but require a refit with
`lean=False` for residuals or covariance recalculation.

```{python}
data = pf.get_data()
compact = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1", data, store_data=False)
compact.vcov("hetero")
compact.vcov({"CRV1": "f1"}, data=data)
compact.predict(newdata=data.head())
```

Supplemental covariance data must preserve the original positional row index
(the index after resetting the input once before fitting). It may include
excluded rows and be reordered; rows are selected by their retained identities.
A filtered frame with a newly reset index cannot safely identify the sample.
IID and heteroskedastic covariance need only retained numerical state. Cluster
and HAC updates need supplemental cluster/time columns when raw data was
omitted. CRV3 refits with absorbed effects require retained raw data.
Default `fixef()` formats retained coefficients when raw data was omitted;
nondefault recovery tolerances require a fit with `store_data=True`.

## Ownership ledger for the published components

The table records the fields migrated in this change. Counts, coefficient
selection metadata, inference, fit geometry, and completed fit products remain
separate work.

| Former model fields | Meaning/domain | Writer and lifetime | Readers and destination |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_model_matrix`, `_fe`, `_weights_df`, `_offset_df`, `_Y_untransformed` | Formula-materialized roles, including the original response | Formula preparation; replaced by `without_rows()` after separation; omitted by existing storage options | Preparation, performance, clustering, and recovery read `model_matrix`; public tables are detached copies of its private storage. The duplicate response copy is removed. |
| `_observation_weights`, `_weights` | User-scale analytic/frequency weights | Formula preparation; retained with numerical state, omitted for lean models | Fitting, covariance, recovery, decomposition, and randomization read `observation_weights`. Consumers that need unit weights allocate them locally. |
| `_within_data`, `_X`, `_Y`, IV `_Z` and `_endogvar` | Unpremultiplied within response, selected design, instruments and endogenous regressors | Demeaning/column selection; retained until lean cleanup | Fitting, inference, first stages, and post-estimation read `within_data`; cache buffers are shared only after protection. |
| `_working_state`, GLM `_X`, `_Y`, `_Z`, `_irls_weights`, `_Xbeta`, `_u_hat_response`, `_u_hat_working`, `_u_hat`, `_Y_hat_link`, `_Y_hat_response` | Final working arrays, means, predictors and residual domains | IRLS completion; retained until lean cleanup | GLM covariance, residuals, performance and prediction read `working_state`. Iteration scratch remains writable. |
| `_offset` | Formula-scale evaluated offset | Formula preparation | Fixed-effect recovery reads the offset role of `model_matrix`. |

The former private names above are removed; they are not compatibility
properties. Model labels and existing formula/selection metadata remain
standalone. Existing fitting and inference lifecycle methods are unchanged in
this step.
